A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BPDQ work. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching, including the additional tables in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization benchmark results, system measurements, and activation analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model and quantization-method comparisons in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same bit-plane initialization, weighted coefficient fitting, iterative bit-plane updates, and delta correction. Equations 1–9 and the quantization procedure are unchanged.

E1.justification: C4 calibration, the seven standard evaluation benchmarks, and the LongBench task subset are unchanged. Tables 6–7 evaluate additional model configurations on existing tasks without adding datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 7 substantially expands the evaluated comparator set with Any-Precision LLM, ShiftAddLLM, AQLM, and QuIP# at 2 and 3 bits. These methods were not evaluated in v1; the existing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Tables 6–7 substantially broaden evaluated model configurations to Llama3.1-8B, Gemma2-9B, Phi4-14B, and LLaMA2-7B. Table 6 also introduces 4-bit comparisons using GPTQ-G32 and AnyBCQ/BPDQ-G64, whereas the original tables use GPTQ-G64 and BPDQ-G128. Existing experiments retain their reported protocols.

E4.justification: The activation-outlier analysis and LongBench stress tests are retained with unchanged findings. Tables 6–7 extend standard benchmark comparisons; no new ablation, sensitivity, robustness, or error analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 6–7 add substantial benchmark and cost evidence. For example, Table 6 reports BPDQ-W2-G64 GSM8K accuracies of 15.92%, 25.63%, and 66.19% on Llama3.1-8B, Gemma2-9B, and Phi4-14B. These are newly reported configurations; Tables 1–5 and existing LongBench scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendices A and B retain the same assumptions, propositions, proofs, and Equations 10–32. Section 3.2 changes 'affine' to 'linear' when describing coefficient dependence, without changing the existing mathematical parameterization or reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims about fixed-grid restrictions, variable-grid expressivity, Hessian-consistent optimization, and single-RTX-3090 deployment of Qwen2.5-72B with 83.85% GSM8K accuracy. Abstract edits do not substantively change these contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations linking variable grids to fidelity and outlier preservation remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same fidelity gap relative to vector quantization and the same proposed enhancements and hardware directions.

D1.justification: Figure 3 newly labels GPTQ-G32 and BPDQ-G64, and Table 6 supplies cost measurements for the added models. Implementation, damping, iteration count, and hardware descriptions remain unchanged. The reformatted GitHub link points to the same repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations and bibliography entries for UnComp and ParallelComp, supporting the existing outlier and long-context discussions. The Related Work section and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract, changes 'affine' to 'linear,' updates affiliation and publication text, and adds acknowledgments. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7 and revises Figure 3 by repeating the existing 16-bit reference bars in the 2-bit and 3-bit panels, adjusting axes, and adding group-size labels. Figures 1–2 and the existing table displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 broaden empirical validation across additional model families and quantization methods, while Figure 3 makes comparison with full precision easier. The benefit is limited by the sparse setup and interpretation accompanying the new tables. The method, proofs, and original results remain intact, yielding a useful but bounded overall improvement.
